items.prompt: Ridge regression adds which term to the least-squares loss?
choices: A hinge-loss term
λ‖w‖₁, the L1 norm of the weights
The log-determinant of XᵀX
λ‖w‖₂², the squared L2 norm of the weights
items.explain: Ridge penalizes the squared L2 norm, shrinking weights toward zero. The L1 penalty is the lasso.

items.prompt: The ridge solution is w = (XᵀX + λI)⁻¹Xᵀy. Why does adding λI help when features are collinear?
choices: It forces w to be sparse
It rescales y to unit variance
It lifts every eigenvalue of XᵀX by λ, so the matrix becomes invertible and well conditioned
It deletes the collinear columns
items.explain: Collinearity makes XᵀX singular or nearly so. Adding λI shifts all eigenvalues up by λ > 0.

items.prompt: Ridge regression is the MAP estimate under which prior on the weights?
choices: A Laplace prior
A Dirichlet prior
A uniform prior over a box
A zero-mean Gaussian prior
items.explain: A Gaussian prior adds a squared L2 term to the negative log posterior; a Laplace prior gives the lasso.

items.prompt: A Gaussian process is fully specified by…
choices: a set of weights and biases
a transition matrix
a mean function and a covariance (kernel) function
a finite list of basis functions
items.explain: Any finite set of GP values is jointly Gaussian, so the mean and covariance functions determine everything.

items.prompt: With matched noise and prior, the GP posterior mean equals the prediction of…
choices: k-nearest neighbours
a decision tree
lasso regression
kernel ridge regression with the same kernel
items.explain: Both solve the same linear system (K + σ²I)α = y; the GP adds a posterior variance on top.

items.prompt: Exact GP regression on n training points costs O(n³) mainly because of…
choices: evaluating the mean function
evaluating the kernel at test points
sampling hyperparameters
factoring or solving with the n×n kernel matrix
items.explain: A Cholesky factorization of the n×n kernel matrix is cubic in n and dominates the cost.

items.prompt: In the infinite-width limit (NTK parameterization), gradient-descent training of a network behaves like…
choices: a random walk that never converges
k-means clustering
kernel regression with a fixed kernel, the NTK
training a decision tree
items.explain: At infinite width the tangent kernel stays constant during training, so the dynamics are those of kernel regression.

items.prompt: Why is the 'lazy' NTK regime considered a limited model of deep learning?
choices: It cannot fit the training data
It only applies to convolutional networks
Features barely move during training, so it cannot capture feature learning
It only works for binary labels
items.explain: In the lazy regime the representation is frozen at initialization; real networks gain much of their power by learning features.

items.prompt: In deep linear networks trained from small initialization, the singular modes of the input–output map are learned…
choices: one after another, strongest first, giving stage-like drops in the loss
in random order unrelated to their strength
all at exactly the same rate
never, since linear networks cannot learn
items.explain: Saxe et al. show each mode follows a sigmoidal trajectory whose timing scales inversely with its singular value.

choices: a filter that removes everything above the Nyquist frequency
an adaptive filter driven by error signs
the linear filter that minimizes mean-squared error for stationary signals
a nonlinear maximum-likelihood filter
items.explain: Wiener filtering is optimal linear MSE estimation given the signal and noise spectra.

items.prompt: The Kalman filter alternates which two steps?
choices: Forward and backward smoothing passes
Encode and decode
Sample and reject
Predict (propagate the state) and update (correct with the measurement)
items.explain: Each cycle propagates mean and covariance through the model, then corrects them with the new measurement.

items.prompt: As the measurement-noise covariance R grows, the Kalman gain…
choices: becomes negative
stays the same
grows, so the filter trusts measurements more
shrinks, so the filter trusts its model prediction more
items.explain: The gain weighs prediction uncertainty against measurement noise; noisier measurements get less weight.

items.prompt: For linear-Gaussian systems the Kalman filter is exactly optimal because…
choices: its gain is fixed in advance
it uses many particles
the posterior stays Gaussian, so its mean and covariance update in closed form
it ignores the noise
items.explain: Linear maps of Gaussians are Gaussian, so the full posterior is carried by two moments.
